intro:
Howdy all! With September well underway, we hope everyone is finding their groove this semester.

We have another great discussion lined up **this Friday**: ERC Steering Committee member Dr. John Williams III is taking on our latest PEP Talk. He’ll explore critical questions about discipline, literacy, and opportunity for Black boys.

Thanks for tuning in!

Want to feature something in an upcoming newsletter? [**Let us know here!**](https://erc-policy-exchange.vercel.app/share/)

fields.title: Howdy, Neighbor: Do Peer Mentors Keep First-Year Aggies on Track?
fields.summary: Can a sophomore with a clipboard change a freshman's trajectory? Among 12,000 first-year students at a large Texas university, those matched with a trained peer mentor during their first semester were 6 percentage points more likely to return for year two. Gains were largest for first-generation students and students from rural high schools, a low-cost program with outsized staying power.

fields.title: Miles from Aggieland: Distance to Dual-Credit Programs in Rural Texas
fields.summary: For students in the Brazos Valley's smallest towns, the nearest dual-credit partner campus can be an hour away. Tracking 90,000 fictional high schoolers, this brief shows each additional 15 minutes of drive time cuts dual-credit enrollment by 9 percent, and that a modest travel stipend closes most of the gap.

fields.title: Maroon and White and Certified All Over: Alternative Teacher Certification in Texas
fields.authors: Kate Sample, Andy Fictional & Brenden Placeholder
fields.summary: This report evaluates a statewide alternative certification pathway serving 3,200 fictional candidates. Completers were as likely as traditionally certified peers to remain in teaching after three years, and more likely to teach in high-need rural districts, though early-career observation scores lagged in the first year before catching up.

fields.title: ERC PEP Talk with John Williams III
fields.summary:
Please join the ERC and the [**Program in Education in Policy**](https://pep.tamu.edu/) for the first PEP Talk of the academic year, featuring **Dr. John Williams III. **Attendees may join via Zoom.

Come hungry; lunch and refreshments will be provided!

fields.title: ERC EdTalk: Dr. Rowan Vale on Rural School Finance
fields.summary:
Dr. Vale studies how small districts stretch a dollar: what happens to course offerings, staffing, and facilities when enrollment falls and the formula does not follow. This talk previews a new paper on 140 fictional rural districts and what the next legislative session could change.

Lunch will be provided. RSVP by October 6.

fields.title: Resource Spotlight: Federal Data at Texas A&M
fields.summary:
Thank you to Dr. Mary Campbell, Director of the **[Texas Research Data Center (TXRDC)](https://liberalarts.tamu.edu/txrdc/)**, for joining us for our first talk of the semester.

The TXRDC works with the U.S. Census Bureau to host a secure lab at Texas A&M where approved researchers can use restricted-access federal data. For education researchers, that means versions of the American Community Survey, Current Population Survey, and decennial census with larger samples, finer geography, more detailed variables, and links between datasets that public files don't allow. Texas A&M leads the TXRDC Consortium, so our researchers can run funded projects at reduced lab fees, and in many cases the fees are waived.

Curious whether your project is a fit? Dr. Campbell and Dr. Karin Johnson will cover what data are available and how to apply for access at an informational session this Thursday. Details below under Upcoming Events.

fields.title: Civil Discourse Symposium: Talking Across the Aisle About Schools
fields.summary: A half-day of panels on how school boards, legislators, and researchers argue productively about evidence. ERC faculty join a panel on what administrative data can and cannot settle. Open to students, staff, and the public.

fields.title: AI, Memory, and Student Privacy in K–12 Education
fields.summary: Education-specific artificial intelligence (AI) tools ask teachers and students to submit personal information that the models then "remember" to improve results. Experts in AI technology, data sharing, and education discuss who owns and controls those memories, whether they can be edited or transferred, and how states are handling the complexities. Hosted by the American Enterprise Institute (AEI).

fields.title: What Schools Need to Know About the Federal Education Freedom Tax Credit
fields.summary: Cecilia Retelle Zywicki, CEO of LearningSpring, walks through the federal Education Freedom Tax Credit (EFTC), which launches January 1, 2027 and lets eligible taxpayers redirect $1,700 of federal tax liability to Scholarship Granting Organizations. Funds support K-12 students in public, private, faith-based, and charter settings through scholarships and academic services, with guidance for school and district leaders on preparing.

fields.title: Portraits of Progress: How States Can Reduce Chronic Absenteeism
fields.summary: Chronic absenteeism remains above pre-pandemic levels, though rates are declining modestly nationwide. The American Enterprise Institute's (AEI) Nat Malkus reports the latest numbers, then Iowa Department of Education Director McKenzie Snow and Rhode Island Education Commissioner Angélica Infante-Green discuss the policies driving outsize progress in their states. Cohosted with Attendance Works and the Education Trust; audience Q&A follows.

fields.title: Unlearning to Teach Mathematics
fields.summary: Dr. Deborah Loewenberg Ball opens the Curtis D. Robert Distinguished Speaker Series in STEM Education Research with a talk on how future teachers' prior experiences shape their assumptions about teaching and learning, and how teacher preparation can support unlearning and rebuilding those understandings. Organized by Dr. Jinfa Cai and Dr. Trina Davis.

fields.title: Superintendent (In)Stability and Student Achievement in the United States
fields.summary: Superintendents shape conditions for teaching and learning, yet the limited studies of their impact—concentrated in a few states and focused on superintendent turnover—find small or null effects on student achievement. Using more than 37,000 district-year records from national superintendents and student achievement datasets, and drawing on organizational learning and managerial succession… more →

fields.title: Unequal Foundations: Racial Disparities in School Building Conditions in New York State
fields.summary: School infrastructure is a critical yet often overlooked factor shaping student health, learning, and well-being. This study examines racial disparities in public school building conditions across New York State using building inspection data linked to demographic and fiscal data. Schools serving more students of color are significantly more likely to have poor overall conditions, inadequate ventilation, mold exposure, and reduced access to athletic fields, gymnasiums, and health offices. A Kitagawa-Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition shows that local property taxes are the largest contributor to racial gaps in building quality, while progressive state building aid helps reduce these disparities. These findings highlight persistent infrastructure inequities and the need for targeted investments to ensure all students have access to safe and healthy learning environments.

fields.title: The Post-Pandemic “Attendance Crisis” in Historical Perspective
fields.summary: School attendance rates in the United States are lower now than prior to the COVID-19 pandemic. This rise in absenteeism has often been characterized as a crisis; but whether it amounts to a broader breakdown in norms depends on the historical baseline against which it is judged.
